options: the maintenance of a constant internal environment
the removal of waste products of metabolism
the maintenance of a constant external environment
the conversion of glucose to glycogen
questions.why: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant internal environment, by negative feedback.

questions.q: Blood glucose concentration rises after a meal. What happens next?
options: The liver converts glycogen into glucose.
The pancreas secretes insulin; the liver converts glucose into glycogen.
The liver secretes insulin into the blood.
questions.why: Insulin from the pancreas causes the liver to store glucose as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

questions.q: On a hot day, what happens in the skin?
options: Arterioles supplying skin capillaries dilate, so more heat is lost.
Blood vessels move closer to the skin surface.
questions.why: Vasodilation of arterioles sends more blood through surface capillaries; vessels do not move.

questions.q: Explain how sweating cools the body.
questions.model: Water in sweat evaporates from the skin surface, transferring heat energy away from the skin.
points: heat energy transferred away from the skin
